narrative.heading: Writing and learning about relationships
narrative.text: Before her counseling career, Stacy Notaras Murphy worked as a business writer and editor. Her biography says she began bringing those reporting skills to psychology writing in 2005, when she became a regular contributor to Counseling Today. She describes an interest in relationships leading into couples work and later study of trauma’s effects on relationships. She also describes meeting with other therapists for consultation and support.

access.heading: Before arranging care
access.text: Her FAQ lists in-person sessions at a Dupont Circle office and telehealth for residents of DC or Virginia; Maryland residents are seen in person only. The reviewed page does not establish a street address. It lists $250 for individual 50-minute sessions and $315 for 55-minute couples/family sessions, observed October 15, 2026. The page describes an out-of-network model, full payment at service, and monthly statements that may support reimbursement; reimbursement is not guaranteed. Current appointment capacity and age eligibility are not established.

narrative.heading: Writing, teaching and relationship patterns
narrative.text: Kathleen Smith’s biography describes writing a therapy newsletter as one of her favorite parts of the work week. It also describes talking with friends about relationships in television shows and teaching family-systems ideas to clinicians and other professional groups. The profile keeps these documented writing, interest and teaching details separate from claims about treatment results.

access.heading: Therapy access and separate services
access.text: Her therapy page lists an office at 1900 L Street NW, Washington, DC, and says she also sees clients virtually. She says she does not accept insurance directly but can provide documentation for possible out-of-network reimbursement for DC residents or people seen in DC; reimbursement is not guaranteed. The site separately describes virtual Bowen Theory coaching/consulting for people worldwide. That coaching geography does not establish therapy eligibility outside DC. Current therapy-location eligibility, capacity, fees and age eligibility are not established.
